outcomes.description: Change the DVD from black to white.

nodes.question: Can the DVD visible in the source image be identified in the edited image, and what is its color there?
nodes.criteria: Track the same DVD from the source into the edited image using its position, shape, and visible details; do not identify it solely by proximity to another disc. Complete only if the same DVD is visibly white. Partial only if the same DVD is identifiable and visibly changed from black toward white but is not yet white. Absent if the same DVD is identifiable and remains black without a requested color change. If the source DVD is missing, or its identity or color change cannot be established, use unknown; disappearance and a nearby or newly appearing disc are not progress.
nodes.binding: Source target: the small square DVD case near the center of the source image, with a visible printed face. Track that same object across the edit using its shape, position, and details. Do not treat either nearby white circular disc in the edited image as the target unless visual evidence establishes it is the same DVD.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
